name: Suzanne Jimenez
title: Chief of Staff, Service Employees International Union - United Healthcare Workers West
background: Jimenez is Chief of Staff of SEIU-United Healthcare Workers West (SEIU-UHW), the healthcare workers' union that sponsors Proposition 40 on the November 2026 California ballot. She and Jim Mangia, President and CEO of St. John's Community Health, filed the Proposition 40 initiative with the California Attorney General on October 22, 2025 as co-proponents; the measure was cleared for signature circulation on December 26, 2025. Proposition 40 would impose a one-time 5 percent excise tax on the net worth of California residents whose covered assets exceeded $1 billion on January 1, 2026, directing 90 percent of the resulting revenue, which the Legislative Analyst's Office estimates at tens of billions of dollars, to health care including Medi-Cal, and the remaining 10 percent to K-14 education and food assistance. (Source: content/measures/ca-prop-40-2026.json in this voter guide.)

Jimenez signed the official ballot argument in favor of Proposition 40 in the state's Voter Information Guide, alongside Victoria Barron of Planned Parenthood of Pacific Southwest and Denise Robb of the American Federation of Teachers Local 1521. She also signed SEIU-UHW's official ballot arguments against the competing Propositions 41 and 42 — both funded chiefly by Building a Better California, whose largest donor is Google co-founder Sergey Brin — arguing that those measures' same-ballot conflict clauses are designed to nullify Proposition 40's wealth tax if either outpolls it rather than to serve the transparency and taxpayer-protection purposes stated in their ballot titles. (Source: content/measures/ca-prop-40-2026.json, ca-prop-41-2026.json, and ca-prop-42-2026.json in this voter guide.)

I was not able to independently verify further biographical detail about Jimenez — her education, prior career history, or how long she has held her position at SEIU-UHW — through the public sources available during this research. SEIU-UHW's own website returned repeated 403 (access denied) responses to both direct and proxied requests for its leadership and press pages; Ballotpedia, which would ordinarily carry a proponent profile, was unreachable throughout this research, consistent with a known access problem flagged for this project; and this research session's web search tool had exhausted its query budget by the time her profile was researched, which prevented broader news-archive searches beyond the small set of Google News results already surfaced (none of which, on inspection, contained biographical detail about her beyond her title and role in the Proposition 40 campaign). This profile is therefore limited to what her title, role, and public campaign activity establish, rather than a fuller career biography.
